top_stories.title: Anthropic's record IPO loses steam amid broader tech selloff
points: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83/share, raising $81.3 billion—the largest IPO on record, surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion June offering.
Stock opened around $111.50, briefly valuing the AI company at $2 trillion fully diluted (accounting for all potential share conversions) before settling near $1.27 trillion market cap.
Shares closed up 17.1% on debut day, but slipped on day two as broader tech/AI stocks sold off, with Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all falling over 2% the day Anthropic began trading.
Combined wealth of Anthropic founders and employees now exceeds that of one-third of U.S. households.

Retail investor enthusiasm was notably weaker than for SpaceX: net buying of just $19 million in the first 30 minutes (vs. SpaceX's $26 million), widening to $37 million vs. $99 million after three hours, despite higher total trading volume ($820 million vs. $669 million) suggesting more tactical selling.
S&P 500 fell for 6 consecutive trading days, with futures plunging further Friday morning; Nasdaq futures were down roughly 1.4-1.7%.
Taiwan's benchmark stock index posted its worst week since 1991 amid a global AI sector selloff.
Gold fell 2.6% to $3,590.60 and Bitcoin dropped 3.5% to $61,738, reflecting broad risk-off sentiment across asset classes.
DayOne Data Centers postponed a multibillion-dollar IPO, citing concerns over elevated AI infrastructure valuations (the price investors assign to companies).

unique_angles.point: Nasdaq dominated 2026 IPO activity broadly, raising $201.8B across 64 listings (10x NYSE's $20.8B across 42 listings), with NDAQ stock up 21% year-over-year partly due to hosting both Anthropic's and SpaceX's mega-IPOs.
Anthropic's debut coincided with a short-seller report on AMD alleging improper firmware sales to a blacklisted Chinese firm, sending AMD down 7.7% and compounding AI-sector headwinds the same day.

Anthropic's valuation intensifies S&P 500 concentration risk, as the top 10 companies now represent 40% of index value; the equal-weighted S&P 500 is up 11% this year vs. just 6% for the market-cap-weighted version.
Global equities are on track for their longest losing streak in more than three years as the AI trade unravels, with Anthropic's IPO failing to lift Asian markets on day two.
Framed the move as a broad 'tech wreck' dragging down both established tech firms and newly public companies like Anthropic simultaneously.

items.title: Kalshi hires GTA VI researcher amid flood of applications

items.title: Roaring Kitty's cryptic post sends GameStop up 3%
points: Keith Gill (Roaring Kitty) posted a single image—Mario as an excited cat—on X after nearly two years of silence, with no accompanying commentary.
GameStop shares jumped 3% on the post and are up over 30% year-to-date, outperforming several mega-cap tech stocks despite weak underlying fundamentals.

items.title: Micron warns of worsening memory chip shortages
points: Micron warned that memory chip supply constraints will worsen, adding to broader tech supply chain concerns.

items.title: US nears ban on Chinese automakers
points: US lawmakers are close to a deal banning Chinese automakers like BYD and Geely from the US market, while last-minute talks aim to spare Mercedes-Benz, which is nearly 20% Chinese-owned.

points: New fees and processing delays are causing H-1B visa holders (specialized workers sponsored by US employers) to abandon US tech jobs.

points: Gas prices fell to an 8-month low after 26 consecutive days of declines, offering relief to consumers at the pump.

issues.subject: Nasdaq Claims The Year Of The Mega-IPO

sections.title: Nasdaq's IPO Victory: Structural Advantages Drive High-Growth Listings
points: 64 Nasdaq IPOs raised $201.8 billion in 2026, compared to 42 NYSE IPOs raising just $20.8 billion—a roughly 10x advantage in capital raised.
Nasdaq stock (NDAQ) climbed 21% over the past year and 92% over three years, nearly double the 48% return of NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE).
Nasdaq attracts disruptors through lower listing fees, more flexible entry requirements, faster IPO processing, and access to benchmarks like the Nasdaq-100 (NDX).
Exchange recently loosened rules to fast-track large IPOs like SpaceX directly into major indices to boost liquidity and broaden shareholder bases.

Stock traded higher on debut but then slipped, indicating volatility and investor caution despite the "historic" nature of the listing.

headlines: Anthropic's record $81.3 billion IPO failed to lift the AI trade—instead, the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all fell over 2% on the company's first trading day, with shares ending up 17.1%.

Short seller Hunterbrook Media published a negative report on AMD alleging improper firmware sales to a blacklisted Chinese firm, sending AMD shares down 7.7% despite the chipmaker's recent 45% rally.

JPMorgan now expects the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates by a quarter-point at each of the next three meetings (December, January, and March), with markets pricing in a near-certain December hike.
Jobless claims unexpectedly rose to 203,000 last week versus economist expectations of 197,000, with continuing claims hitting their highest level since late August at 1.763 million.
Walmart raised its full-year sales growth guidance to 4.9–5.2% from 4–5%, but its stock fell 1% as CEO flagged higher diesel costs.

sections.title: Anthropic IPO Backfires as Market Rotates Out of AI
points: 1. Anthropic priced at $83 per share in a $81.3 billion offering Wednesday, topping SpaceX's $75 billion June IPO as the largest on record.
2. Stock opened at $111.50 near noon, valuing the company at $2 trillion on a fully diluted basis (accounting for all potential share conversions), and closed up 17.1% on day one.
3. The IPO triggered immediate selling across AI stocks: the market declined sharply as Anthropic started trading, suggesting investors rotated capital out of existing AI holdings into the new stock.
4. The timing coincided with negative AMD coverage, creating a two-pronged headwind: loss of a 'safer AI trade' narrative while capital was absorbed by Anthropic's debut.

sections.title: AMD Faces Short Attack Despite Strong Recent Rally
points: 1. Hunterbrook Media reported that AMD firmware versions continued appearing at IEIT Systems, a Chinese firm blacklisted by the U.S. in 2025, raising compliance concerns.
2. Hunterbrook Capital, an affiliated fund, holds a short position in AMD, creating a potential conflict of interest in the report's credibility.
3. AMD rejected the allegations, saying the report 'misrepresents AMD's business practices and relationships'; shares fell 7.7% to $489.19 on the news.
4. The drop is significant given AMD rallied nearly 45% from November 5–12 following Nvidia's leadership turmoil, making it the perceived beneficiary of Nvidia's crisis.

sections.title: Labor Market Shows Unexpected Weakness
points: 1. Initial jobless claims rose 1,000 to 203,000, beating economist forecasts of 197,000, signaling a potential softening in employment.
2. Continuing claims (people receiving benefits for more than one week) jumped 70,000 to 1.763 million, the highest level since late August.
3. The data arrives as the Fed prepares for interest rate hikes, complicating the central bank's inflation-fighting narrative if employment deteriorates.

issues.subject: Morning Brief: People treated Anthropic way differently than SpaceX

headlines: Anthropic's IPO valued the AI lab at $1.27 trillion after opening 34% above its $83 IPO price, the largest IPO ever at $81 billion raised, though markets fell 1.4-1.7% as tech stocks continued declining.

Retail investors showed dramatically less interest in Anthropic than SpaceX's June IPO—$19 million net buying in the first 30 minutes versus SpaceX's $26 million—despite higher total trading volume suggesting more selling pressure.
Kalshi hired a GTA VI researcher after receiving 33,000 applications, selecting content creator Cliff Savage to livestream and study the game's economy ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI's launch.
Keith Gill (Roaring Kitty) posted a single image for the first time in nearly two years, causing GameStop stock to jump 3% and reinforcing the stock's 30% year-to-date gain.
Major US companies and payment systems JPMorgan, Visa, and Mastercard disclosed cyberattacks on vendors, while Micron warned memory chip supply constraints will worsen.

sections.title: Anthropic's $1.27 Trillion Valuation Ties US Markets to AI Concentration Risk
points: Anthropic (ANT) opened at $111.50, 34% above the $83 IPO price, briefly hitting $2 trillion market cap before settling at $1.27 trillion, making it one of the most valuable companies instantly.

The IPO amplifies an existing problem: the top 10 companies represent 40% of the S&P 500's value, so losses in big tech names drag down the entire market—the S&P 500 fell 1.4% Thursday despite Anthropic's surge.

AI has deepened this concentration as tech giants pour massive investments into AI operations and their supply chains (chipmakers, power generators, data centers), making Anthropic's entry as a primary AI tool supplier even more systemically important.
The equal-weighted S&P 500 is up 11% this year versus the market-weighted version at only 6%, illustrating how much the index is driven by a handful of mega-cap names.

sections.title: Retail Investors Show Less Enthusiasm for Anthropic Than SpaceX Despite Larger Trading Volume
points: In Anthropic's first 30 minutes, retail net buying was $19 million versus SpaceX's $26 million in June; by three hours, the gap widened to $37 million versus $99 million, suggesting weaker retail conviction.

Total trading volume tells a different story: Anthropic saw $820 million in total volume (buys plus sells) versus SpaceX's $669 million, indicating retail investors were more willing to sell into strength or trade tactically rather than hold.

The discrepancy suggests SpaceX benefited from Elon Musk's outsized brand appeal and cult following, while Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and the company lack comparable cultural cachet despite leading the AI frontier.
Retail investors appeared to view Anthropic as a "win the market" trading opportunity rather than a long-term conviction buy, contrasting with SpaceX's broader bull market sentiment.

sections.title: Kalshi's GTA VI Researcher Hire Reflects AI-Powered Hiring at Scale
points: Kalshi received 33,000 applications for one job posting to livestream and analyze Grand Theft Auto VI's economy, highlighting extreme competition for novel roles and intense public interest in the game's midnight Thursday launch.

Selected candidate Cliff Savage is a recording artist and streamer with 16,000 monthly Spotify listeners and 2,000+ Twitch followers, suggesting the role attracted established content creators seeking new revenue streams.

The hiring process likely used AI screening to handle the 33,000-application volume, with many applications possibly AI-generated, illustrating how both job seekers and employers now deploy AI as standard tools in talent acquisition.
This moment reflects broader labor market trends where getting a resume to a human reviewer is becoming a success metric itself amid AI-driven recruitment automation.

sections.title: Keith Gill Returns to Social Media, Triggering GameStop Rally
points: After nearly two years of silence, Roaring Kitty (Keith Gill) posted a single image on X—a picture of Mario as an excited cat—with no additional commentary, causing GameStop to immediately jump 3%.

GameStop is up over 30% year-to-date, outperforming Nvidia, Google, Amazon, and nearly matching Apple despite being a struggling video game retailer, driven largely by retail trader enthusiasm tied to Gill's earlier 2021 short squeeze.

The post provided no new investment thesis, earnings data, or business updates, underscoring how completely GameStop's valuation depends on retail sentiment and Gill's symbolic influence rather than fundamental metrics.

The reemergence of Gill injected excitement into a market that saw broad tech sector weakness, with traders apparently viewing his return as a potential catalyst despite the ambiguous nature of his message.
